commitResults.messageBody:
Properties share the client Buyer/Seller type even though each property
represents a buying or selling action.

Introduce PropertyIntention with Buying and Selling values and accept
them case-insensitively in property commands. Reject client-role values
without changing client intentions.

Keep the existing saved Buyer/Seller representation at the storage
boundary so this change remains compatible with saved data. Leave the
canonical storage migration to the next phase.

Align command help and regression coverage with the new property values.

Saved properties use Buyer/Seller labels even though property intentions
represent Buying/Selling actions.

Write canonical Buying/Selling values and accept legacy Buyer/Seller
values when loading so existing files remain usable across the change.

Reject invalid stored intentions through the existing exception path.
Preserve client intentions, property order and unrelated saved fields.

Property commands use Buying/Selling and saved files accept legacy
Buyer/Seller values, but the guides still describe the old property
syntax.

Align help, examples and manual checks with the property-specific
intention model and its saved-data compatibility rules.

Show PropertyIntention separately from the client role in the existing
model class diagram so the documented model matches the implementation.

Clients store a manual Buyer/Seller role that can disagree with their
properties.

Derive Buyer, Seller, Both or Not specified from the current property
list and reject direct client intention fields in add and edit.

Ignore legacy saved client roles and omit the redundant field from new
saves so properties remain the source of truth across reloads.

Preserve client identity and immutable property-copy semantics when
property commands change the derived role.

Intention searches match only exact client roles, excluding clients who
have both buying and selling properties.

Include Both clients in buyer and seller searches after exact-role
matches, and support a Both-only query.

Use one displayed order for the UI and index-based commands so edits and
deletions target the client shown. Keep each role group in source order
after property changes.

Restore normal order for other searches and list, and preserve the
underlying and saved client order.

The guides still describe a manually assigned client role and omit the
ordering rules for derived intention searches.

Align help, guides, use cases and manual tests with property-derived
roles, search ordering and displayed client indexes. Update the model
UML to show the derived role separately from property intention.

Document legacy client-role compatibility and verify that loading leaves
old files unchanged while saving omits the obsolete client role.

Properties have no recorded transaction stage, so agents cannot track
progress independently for each entry.

Add six property statuses and default existing constructors and legacy
saved properties to Unspecified. Display the recorded stage and preserve
it when editing other property fields.

Persist canonical status names and reject invalid saved values through
the existing storage exceptions. Cover legacy loading, status round
trips, edit preservation and card display with regression tests.

Properties can store a transaction stage, but addp and editp cannot set
or correct it.

Accept optional status on add and allow status-only or combined edits.
Preserve omitted values, reject empty or invalid status, and require an
explicit unspecified token to reset the stage. Allow corrections between
all stages without removing or locking completed properties.

Log successful status changes at FINE with displayed indexes and enum
transitions only. Verify command, persistence, display and logging
behavior, including rejected requests and unchanged edits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find: Filter clients by property status
commitResults.messageBody:
Property stages are recorded, but client searches cannot select them.

Add case-insensitive status searches for all six stages. Match a client
once when any existing property has the requested status, and exclude
clients without properties from unspecified results.

Preserve source order and replace the previous filter without changing
stored clients. Verify existing selectors, live property updates,
displayed indexes and state preservation after rejected queries.

The guides and bundled help omit property stages and status searches,
leaving their defaults and correction rules unclear.

Document all six stages, including the different meanings of Viewing for
buying and selling properties. Explain explicit resets, backward
corrections, status matching and legacy persistence defaults.

Align command examples, glossary, use cases and manual checks with the
implemented behavior. Update the model UML to show each property's
status and verify bundled help examples against the real parsers.
Add location filtering to the find command

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge upstream master into property intention
commitResults.messageBody:
The property-intention branch predates the team's location searches,
defensive property-command checks and startup data protection.

Merge upstream master while preserving Buying/Selling property values,
legacy storage migration and the rollback warning. Reconcile help and
glossary conflicts, and adapt location-search test fixtures to the
separate property-intention model.

Cover property edits under location filters and ensure invalid saved
property intentions block startup without overwriting the data file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add sample properties for derived intentions
commitResults.messageBody:
Fresh sample clients have no properties, so every derived intention is
Not specified and intention searches return no sample matches.

Give Alex buying properties, Bernice selling properties and Charlotte
both, while leaving the other clients without properties. Preserve
existing client identities and real saved-data migration behavior.

Cover the four derived roles and buyer, seller and both sample searches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Avoid linear scans in intention search sorting
commitResults.messageBody:
Equal-role comparisons scan the source list with indexOf, repeating
linear work while sorting intention results.

Use an identity-based position lookup, invalidate it on source changes
and rebuild it lazily. Keep stable ties across additions, deletions,
replacements and address-book resets without stale client references.

Cover 1,000 clients with deterministic equality-call counts and retain
the existing displayed-index command regressions.

The derivation flags use broad buying and selling names that do not
express whether a matching property exists.

Rename them to hasBuyingProperty and hasSellingProperty without
changing how client intention is derived.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test status edits that remove filtered clients
commitResults.messageBody:
The logging handler reads a displayed client after the model changes,
so it fails when a status edit removes that client from the filter.

Check the underlying source client when the record is published. Cover
a parsed Viewing-to-Completed edit that empties the status results,
retains the original displayed indexes and emits one FINE record
without personal data. Keep unchanged and rejected-edit checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align status predicate equality and hashing
commitResults.messageBody:
Status predicates compare by the requested status but inherit identity
hash codes, breaking their contract in hash-based collections.

Derive hashCode from status and test equal instances as HashSet keys
for all statuses while retaining unequal-status and matching checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reuse status parsing in find commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Status searches parse tokens directly even though property commands
already share a validated parsing helper.

Route find status values through PropertyParserUtil.parseStatus and
retain find-specific messages, validation order and exception causes.

Derived client roles predate property intention separation, location
search and startup/property-command safeguards on master.

Combine those changes without restoring stored client roles. Keep the
identity-based ordering lookup and canonical property migration; adapt
constructors, sample properties, documentation and test fixtures.

Cover unspecified predicate matching, location/intention search
interaction and error precedence.

Validate 535 tests, Checkstyle, JaCoCo, repository checks and rendered

commitResults.messageTitle: Add location filtering to the find command
commitResults.messageBody:
Agents cannot find clients by locations recorded on their properties.

Allow find l/ to match full or partial location keywords without regard
to case. Return each client once when any of their property locations
matches, using the existing OR behavior for multiple keywords.

Update command help, the user guide and the developer guide glossary
to explain location searches and the related domain terms.

Cover location matching, input validation and filter replacement with
regression tests. Verify all 466 tests and style checks pass with
Gradle check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Normalize location keywords when creating predicates
commitResults.messageBody:
Location filtering repeats blank checks and lowercase conversion for
every property it examines.

Normalize keywords once when constructing the predicate so matching
can reuse the prepared values. Keep case-insensitive substring and OR
matching, and check equality and diagnostic output for normalized input.

Verify the changes with Gradle check, including tests and Checkstyle.

update separate from the location-search feature for focused review.

existing validation rules.

A multiword location can look like an address search even though find
splits whitespace-separated keywords and matches any of them.

parser-to-command test that checks each keyword can match separately
and excludes unrelated locations and clients without properties.
